reconstruction.rule: Every pull request of the snapshot with a frozen brief is a candidate; the newest, by merge time, are examined up to the limit. A candidate is screened from git history alone — its merge commit must exist with exactly one parent, change at least one test file and something besides tests, its brief must name a §4 scope, and the merged change must touch no protected path that scope does not name — then its withheld test files run, in a scratch clone with dependencies installed at each commit, once on the base commit with the merged change’s test side written in and twice on the merged commit. It is admitted only when at least one test passes in both merged-commit runs and did not pass before. Pass-to-pass then adds the existing test files the pre-push hook’s affected-test selection picks, one import edge deep, for the paths the merged change adds or modifies: each runs once on the merged commit and once on the base commit, and a test passing in both is pass-to-pass.
